name: Daily Case Priorities Digest

parameters.content:
## Daily Case Priorities Digest

### How it works

1. The workflow triggers every morning to fetch open tasks, upcoming calendar entries, and firm user data from Clio.
2. It processes and filters these data streams separately, sorting tasks by due date and calendar entries by start date.
3. The filtered tasks and calendar entries are merged and grouped by attorney to prepare daily priorities and deadlines.
4. If any attorney has digest items, the workflow generates personalized morning digest emails for each attorney.
5. Each email send event is logged, and the digest emails are sent out to corresponding attorneys.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure the Clio API base URL and provide API credentials in environment variables or n8n credentials.
- [ ] Set up an email sending service in n8n with valid SMTP credentials for the "Send Morning Digest Email" node.
- [ ] Ensure the "Log Digest Send Event" node workflow is correctly linked to log send events as required.

### Customization

The grouping and formatting of the digest emails can be customized in the "Build Morning Digest Email" node's code. Filters and data requests can also be tailored by adjusting HTTP request query parameters.

## Schedule trigger and data fetch

The initial trigger that starts the workflow on a schedule and fetches open tasks, calendar entries, and firm users from Clio API.

## Process and filter tasks

Split the task records and filter them to keep only tasks with assignees and due dates, then sort by due date.

## Process and filter calendar entries

Split calendar entry records and filter out those with attendees and valid dates, then sort by calendar start date.

## Merge and group items by attorney

Merge the sorted tasks and calendar entries, then group priorities, deadlines and follow-ups by attorney for digest preparation.

## Conditional digest branching

Check if any attorney has items to digest, continue processing those with items or skip if none.

## Prepare and send emails

Split digest by attorney, build personalized emails, log each send event, and send the morning digest email.

nodes.name: When Morning Digest Runs at 7am
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 7am (n8n server timezone) — before the start of the firm's business day. Feeds three parallel fetches: open Clio tasks, upcoming Clio calendar entries, and the firm's user directory (used later to resolve emails). Adjust the cron expression to match when your attorneys actually want this waiting in their inbox, or restrict it to weekdays only (e.g. '0 7 * * 1-5') if a weekend digest isn't useful.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Tasks From Clio API
nodes.notes:
Pulls every task still marked 'pending' in Clio, regardless of attorney — the next few nodes split, filter, and sort it. Same tasks.json request pattern as PAC-59/61, with 'pending' as the status value.

Confirmed against a live Clio account: 'due_at' and 'priority' are valid fields here, but requesting 'assignee{email}' is rejected outright with 'assignee{email} is not a valid field' — Clio doesn't expose a User's email through nested field selection on this endpoint the way it does a Contact's. Only 'assignee{id,name}' is requested; email is resolved afterward by matching the assignee id against 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio'.

'Never Error' is on, and downstream filtering treats a missing/empty 'data' array the same as zero tasks — a Clio outage degrades this branch gracefully instead of failing the whole digest.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61 — reuse it if already deployed.

Returns up to 200 tasks per run. If your firm regularly has more open at once, add a loop over the 'page' parameter.

nodes.name: Fetch Upcoming Calendar Entries From Clio
nodes.notes:
Pulls every calendar entry (hearings, court dates, client appointments) between today and the end of the follow-up window — these are the digest's 'Deadlines' section, distinct from task due dates.

This is Clio's own Calendar Entries resource (developer.clio.com), a separate resource from tasks.json. Confirmed live: a bare date like '2026-08-24' on 'from'/'to' is rejected with 'ArgumentError: An invalid argument was supplied: invalid xmlschema format' — Clio wants a full ISO 8601 datetime, not just a date. Fixed by using $now.startOf('day').toISO() instead of $now.toISODate(); startOf('day') keeps the window anchored to the start of the calendar day regardless of what time the schedule trigger actually fires.

'attendees{email}' is requested directly since Contacts (unlike Users) are commonly allowed to expose email through nested field selection — but this hasn't been confirmed live for this specific endpoint the way tasks.json's 'assignee{email}' was confirmed to fail. If Clio rejects it the same way, remove 'email' from the fields list here; the grouping step already falls back to resolving the attendee's id against 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio' when a direct email isn't present, so the digest keeps working either way.

'Never Error' is on, and downstream filtering treats a missing/empty 'data' array the same as zero entries — if your Clio plan doesn't expose this endpoint, the digest still sends with just the task sections.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the tasks fetch above — no separate calendar credential needed.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users From Clio API
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory once per run — used by 'Group Priorities Deadlines And Follow-ups By Attorney' to resolve a task's assignee id or a calendar entry's attendee id to a real email address. Requesting 'email' works here because /users.json is the primary resource, not a nested association — Clio confirmed live that 'assignee{email}' on tasks.json is rejected ('assignee{email} is not a valid field'), but a top-level field on the User resource itself is fine.

This node has no outgoing connection on the canvas — it's referenced directly by name ($('Fetch Firm Users From Clio')) from the grouping Code node further downstream, since n8n lets any node reference another node's output by name as long as both ran in the same execution.

Same Clio OAuth2 credential as the other two fetches — no separate setup.

'Never Error' is on; if this fetch fails, every task and calendar entry in that run will fail to resolve an email and be silently excluded from the digest — check execution history if a digest goes unexpectedly quiet.

nodes.name: Split Task Records From Response
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per task, so the Filter and Sort nodes downstream can each operate on individual tasks. An empty or missing 'data' array (e.g. after a Clio error) simply produces zero items — the rest of the branch handles that as 'nothing to report', not a failure.

nodes.name: Split Calendar Entries From Response
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per calendar entry. An empty or missing 'data' array simply produces zero items.

nodes.name: Filter Tasks With Assignee And Due Date
nodes.notes: Drops tasks with no assignee id at all, or no due date. This only catches tasks with literally nobody assigned — an assignee that can't be resolved to an email (not found in the firm's user directory) is instead dropped later, in the grouping step. A nonzero drop rate here is worth checking in Clio periodically — it usually means a task needs an assignee or a due date set.

nodes.name: Filter Calendar Entries With Attendee And Date
nodes.notes: Drops calendar entries with no attendee at all, or no start date. An entry whose attendee(s) can't be resolved to an email (no direct email, and no match in the firm's user directory) is instead dropped later, in the grouping step, which tries each attendee in order until one resolves.

nodes.name: Sort Tasks By Due Date Ascending
nodes.notes: Orders tasks oldest-due-first, so within each bucket the digest email lists the most pressing item at the top.

nodes.name: Sort Calendar Entries By Start Date
nodes.notes: Orders calendar entries soonest-first, so the digest's Deadlines section reads chronologically.

nodes.name: Merge Tasks And Calendar Entries Lists
nodes.notes: Appends the sorted task stream (input 1) and the sorted calendar-entry stream (input 2) into one list. The next node tells a task from a calendar entry by shape (due_at+assignee vs start_at+attendees), not by which input it arrived on — append order isn't load-bearing here.

nodes.name: Group Digest Items By Attorney
nodes.notes: The one node that actually groups by attorney, resolves emails, and applies the digest window. References 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio' directly by name (not through a Merge input) to resolve assignee/attendee ids to real email addresses — a task or calendar entry whose id doesn't match anyone in the user directory is silently excluded, same as one with no assignee at all. Tasks whose due date is further out than FIRM_DIGEST_FOLLOWUP_DAYS are also excluded; this is a morning digest, not a full task list.

nodes.name: If Digest Items Exist For Any Attorney
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one attorney has an overdue task, an upcoming calendar entry, or a follow-up task) → build and send digests.
No (every open task and calendar entry is either out of window, or there simply aren't any) → route to Skip. No emails sent.

nodes.name: Skip When No Items To Digest
nodes.notes: No attorney had anything overdue, upcoming, or due this week. Expected on a quiet day — no digest email sent.

nodes.name: Split Digest Items By Attorney
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per attorney who has at least one digest-worthy item — everything downstream builds and sends one attorney's digest email at a time.

nodes.name: Build Styled Morning Digest Email
nodes.notes:
Builds one styled digest email per attorney with three sections (overdue priorities, upcoming deadlines, this-week follow-ups), a star on any task Clio has marked high priority, and a short teaser linking to the full LegalContext Morning Digest product. This is an internal firm email — no client is ever contacted by this workflow.

LEGALCONTEXT_UPSELL_URL is optional — falls back to a generic protomated.com link if unset.

nodes.name: Log Morning Digest Send Event
nodes.notes:
Logs the digest send to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet via the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33). This is internal record-keeping, not a message to a client — opt-out checking doesn't apply here, same as PAC-59/60/61's internal notifications.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

nodes.name: Send Morning Digest Email To Attorneys
nodes.notes:
Delivers the digest to the attorney. Reads all fields explicitly from 'Build Morning Digest Email' rather than $json — the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

description: Fires every morning and pulls two things from Clio in parallel: every open task, and every calendar entry (hearings, court dates, appointments) in the next several days. Splits, filters, and sorts each with native n8n nodes, merges them, then groups by attorney into Priorities (overdue tasks), Deadlines (upcoming calendar entries), and Follow-ups (tasks due this week). Sends each attorney one styled digest email covering all three — skipping silently on quiet days — and logs every send to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet. Entirely internal, no client is ever contacted. Ends with a short teaser for the full LegalContext Morning Digest, which adds case status, billing alerts, and an AI-summarized action list.
